corrected_fields.summary: The BIS Quarterly Review December 2025 covers international banking and financial market developments, with substantial focus on market structure topics including FX derivatives turnover trends from the 2025 Triennial Survey, the cash-futures basis trade dynamics, and the ongoing LIBOR benchmark reform transition in interest rate derivatives markets. The publication examines structural shifts in global FX and IRD markets amid monetary policy changes and identifies clearing concentration as an emerging challenge for EMEs.
corrected_fields.why_it_matters: This BIS publication provides authoritative, source-grounded data on fundamental market structure elements: FX market liquidity conditions, basis trade dynamics, and clearing infrastructure. For traders and risk managers, understanding the cash-futures basis relationship and clearing concentration patterns is essential for assessing funding risks and execution quality in IRD and FX markets.
corrected_fields.macro_context: The research notes shifts in FX trading amid global monetary policy tightening cycles and links volatility challenges to risk-taking behavior. Sovereign yields moderated with monetary easing, while precious metals and USD appreciated.
corrected_fields.market_structure_context: Core market structure content includes: (1) FX market liquidity conditions and non-visible trading patterns, (2) cash-futures basis trade dynamics and XTD positioning, (3) clearing concentration challenges in EME OTC IRD markets, (4) migration of LIBOR-referenced contracts to new benchmarks, (5) broker-dealer and electronic broker landscape in FX execution.
